body:
Nearly one in four healthcare appointments never happens. A systematic review of 105 studies put the average no-show rate at 23%, and in an August poll , 32% of medical groups said rates were higher in 2026 than in 2025, up from 27% a year earlier. Record deductibles are leading patients to second-guess visits they booked six weeks ago. The cost shows up in revenue, but also in a screening that slips or a follow-up that turns into an urgent visit.

This post shows how to build an outbound voice agent on ElevenAgents that calls patients before a visit, verifies their date of birth, and confirms, reschedules, or cancels the appointment in the electronic health record (EHR) during the call. The slot goes back into inventory while there’s still time to fill it. The agent was built with Architect , the assistant inside ElevenAgents, and it can run as a nightly batch or in real time from EHR events.

The approach is already working. Everlywell uses ElevenAgents to remind members about eligible screenings, and it saw a 10% improvement in screening completion versus traditional interactive voice response (IVR), with 3.5x higher conversion among Spanish-speaking members. Ovianta uses ElevenAgents to follow up after treatment proposals, reaching a 68% patient engagement rate, a 25% increase in treatment conversion, and an 83% reduction in manual follow-up calls for clinic staff.

This is the second post in a healthcare series. The first covered an inbound scheduling agent that answers when patients call to book. To run the outbound agent across a whole patient list, care teams can use Campaign Manager, now in ElevenAgents. It handles calling windows, local-time dialing, retries, and voicemail, and it tracks every patient in one funnel from first call to confirmed visit.

## How clinics fight no-shows today

Most practices already run some kind of reminder program. Front-desk staff calling patients by hand is difficult to scale. These types of calls happen only during business hours, using the same people who answer the inbound line, so it stops once the schedule gets busy.

Text and email reminders are inexpensive to run, able to reach everyone, but usually run one way. Engagement drops for older patients and for anyone whose first language isn't the one the text was written in.

Automated IVR calls sit in between these methods. They scale, and they use the phone. However, a “press-1-to-confirm” menu still cannot handle a reschedule, cannot verify identity to any real standard, and hands off badly when the patient asks a question.

Outsourced call centers give you human conversations at volume, but at a high cost-per-call. This approach comes with quality that varies by shift and with more people handling protected health information outside your organization.

The research points one way on delivery: a reminder that reaches the patient live does far better than one that doesn't. A Veterans Health Administration study found a 3% no-show rate when a phone reminder reached the patient live, 24% when it went to voicemail, and 39% when nobody answered and no voicemail was left. For many health systems, only a front-desk call can verify the patient and change the schedule in the same touch, but it doesn't scale. With ElevenAgents, health systems can now proactively reach patients, make real-time changes to their schedule, and scale their outreach.

## What we're building

The outbound reminder agent runs on the same platform, tools, and security review as the inbound scheduling agent, so one vendor covers both the front door and the follow-up. It calls the patient ahead of the visit, confirms their identity, and reads the live appointment from the EHR. From there, it confirms, reschedules, or cancels the appointment against the provider’s open slots.

The agent also handles the edge cases. If the call goes to voicemail, it leaves a message. If a patient asks not to be called again, it records the opt-out so no future calls go out. If a patient wants to talk to a person, it transfers to the front desk. A nightly export can trigger it as a scheduled batch, or real-time EHR events can trigger it one call at a time.

ElevenLabs built this agent with Architect , the assistant inside ElevenAgents that reads and edits an agent’s configuration, workflow, tools, and tests from a chat. The previous post configured every node by hand. This time, the call was described in plain language, and Architect built the workflow.

## Prerequisites

To build the outbound agent, you’ll need:

• An ElevenLabs account with ElevenAgents.

• A Twilio number imported into ElevenAgents, or a SIP trunk.

• A sandbox EHR. We use the public HAPI FHIR R4 server with synthetic patient and appointment records. Nothing real goes on that server; it is world-readable.

• No separate calendar. Scheduling reads and writes the EHR's Schedule, Slot and Appointment resources, the way a practice management system does.

• For the real-time path only: somewhere to run a small trigger service that listens to your EHR and calls the ElevenLabs API. A serverless function is enough.

Seed one synthetic patient and one appointment so the agent has something to remind you about:

Then seed a Schedule for the provider and a handful of free Slots on it: one POST /Schedule , and one POST /Slot per opening with a schedule reference, status free , and a UTC start and end . Keep the three IDs. The patient ID becomes patient_id (and, prefixed with Patient/ , patient_reference ), the appointment ID becomes appointment_id , and the schedule becomes fhir_schedule_id .

The agent is the same no matter how a call starts. What differs is the trigger, which determines freshness, cost and compliance posture.
